transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-17
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Ava (Redwood CSM), Maya (Acme Head of ML), Ethan (CTO), Liam (Data Eng), Priya (Product), Samir (Security)

[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync. quick check — agenda is 1) go over the benchmark results we pushed last night, 2) tuning actions, 3) security/questions, and 4) next steps. sounds good?
[00:00:12] Maya: Yeah that works. thanks.
[00:00:15] Ethan: Good. we have slot for exec summary at the end if possible.
[00:00:20] Jordan: Totally — we'll leave five minutes for that. Sofia can you take us through the results?
[00:00:28] Sofia: Sure. So we ran the three configured workloads: inference throughput with 1k context, median latency tests at 128/256/512 tokens, and the recall/precision eval against the 800 labeled queries you provided. The full spreadsheet link is in the chat — note that the numbers are from the pilot cluster on our hosted Dedicated equivalent.
[00:00:52] Sofia: Highlights — average latency at 256 tokens is ~120ms per request on the xG-8 setup, p99 around 420ms. Token cost per 1k tokens is approximately $0.045 after batching and prefix caching. For the recall metric on the product QA set, we saw recall 0.78 precision 0.84, F1 0.81. Hallucination rate by our automatic detector is roughly 6% on that set.
[00:01:20] Maya: 6% hallucinations — that matches what we saw in user QA sessions. can you break down where hallucinations spike?
[00:01:30] Sofia: Mostly on longer context windows and on product edge-cases where we have sparse training examples. also when prompts include ambiguous SKU references. we'll send per-query failure examples.
[00:01:42] Liam: On the latency piece — 420ms p99 is fine but for our mobile use-case we were hoping sub-300 p99. What's our levers there?
[00:01:52] Sofia: Right — levers are: reduce max tokens (we tested 512, which drops p99 to ~310ms), tweak batching policies to favor latency vs throughput, and possibly use a lower-precision quant profile which gives ~10-15% latency improvement at small accuracy cost. Also local KV cache for short prefixes helps a lot for repeat queries.
[00:02:12] Priya: What's the user-visible impact if we go lower-precision? any noticeable drop in QA quality?
[00:02:18] Sofia: On our test set, going from FP16 to the recommended int8-ish profile changed recall from 0.78 to 0.75; precision stayed about the same. So slight recall hit — that's why we want your labeled edge cases to measure if that impacts your success criteria.
[00:02:34] Maya: Our success criteria are: recall >= 0.80 on priority queries OR reduce human escalations by 40% within pilot. Right now recall is slightly under.
[00:02:44] Jordan: Good to have that explicit. If we can get to 0.80 via prompt tuning + targeted data, that's the fastest path; if not, we can look at more compute or model variant routing in the short term.
[00:02:58] Ethan: On cost — does switching to Dedicated buy us lower unit cost vs hosted? we need a clear delta for the business case.
[00:03:06] Jordan: Yes — Dedicated gives better sustained throughput pricing and you remove multi-tenant overhead. We'll put numbers in the spreadsheet — rough estimate we shared earlier was 20-30% lower per-token at your pilot scale, but we'll firm that up in the revised pricing.
[00:03:20] Samir: Quick security question — what about data residency and KMS? can we lock keys to our cloud project?
[00:03:28] Jordan: Absolutely. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. For hosted we offer encryption at rest and strict retention policies but not customer KMS in the shared offering. We'll share SOC2 docs and our SAML/SSO checklist.
[00:03:44] Samir: Please do — send those to me and our infra team.
[00:03:48] Ava: I'll follow up on that with the link.
[00:03:50] Sofia: Back to tuning — we tried two prompt templates; template B with explicit grounding reduced hallucinations from 6% to 3.8% but added ~30ms to median latency. So there is a tradeoff. Also we noticed repeated queries benefited from prefix caching which reduces end-to-end latency on returning customers.
[00:04:12] Maya: That grounding improvement is promising; can you share the exact template changes?
[00:04:18] Sofia: Yup — we'll push the prompt diffs and a short doc to the drive.
[00:04:22] Liam: For the network — we saw occasional spikes that line up with our bulk export jobs. Is it possible to isolate the pilot traffic or prioritize requests?
[00:04:32] Sofia: You can set routing policies and QoS at the edge via our Dedicated configuration. For the pilot, simplest is to schedule heavy exports off-peak or use a burst bucket to isolate; for longer term we can provision separate GPU pools.
[00:04:48] Ethan: On integration — our engineers need a checklist for deploying the SDK into the mobile backend. can you provide a step-by-step and sample config for VPC peering?
[00:04:58] Jordan: Yes — we have a quickstart doc and sample terraform templates. I'll attach links and Sofia will be available for a follow-up tech session.
[00:05:06] Priya: One ask — can you include a simple ROI calc for the exec deck? compare current human cost for escalations vs predicted reduction at 40%?
[00:05:14] Jordan: We'll include a one-pager ROI.
[00:05:18] Maya: ok great. Any surprises in the benchmark that we should be aware of?
[00:05:24] Sofia: Only thing was one anomalous test run where p99 shot to 1.2s — that was due to a misconfigured batch window on the test harness; we excluded it from the summary but we'll provide the raw logs. Also a few transcription oddities in the automatic logs — names like "Redwood Dedicate" were auto-corrected.
[00:05:42] Liam: Good to know. about the eval set — we'll add the 2k examples and annotate top failure modes.
[00:05:48] Maya: timeline-wise, if we get those examples by 6/23 can we expect a re-run of tuned benchmarks and an exec-ready report by 6/27?
[00:05:58] Sofia: Yes, with the caveat that we need two business days to process and run the targeted tests, so 6/27 is feasible.
[00:06:06] Jordan: Okay recap before we close — Sofia will rerun benchmarks with the 512 token median and include p99 tails and per-query failure logs; she'll also push prompt template diffs. Jordan will send pricing and SOW for a 3-month Dedicated pilot. Acme provides labeled eval set and security questions. Redwood to share SOC2 + SAML docs. We'll schedule exec review for the week of 6/30.
[00:06:28] Ethan: Sounds good.
[00:06:30] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[00:06:32] Jordan: Thanks — meeting adjourned.

Notes/Links shared in chat: benchmark spreadsheet (link), prompt-template-diffs (link), SOC2 and security checklist (link), quickstart VPC peering terraform snippet (link)

End of transcript.
